'''Colm Mulcahy''' (born September 1958) is an Irish mathematician, academic, columnist, book author, public outreach speaker, amateur magician and Professor Emeritus at [[Spelman College]]. In addition to algebra, number theory, and geometry, his interests include [[Mathemagician|mathemagical card magic]] and the culture of mathematics–particularly the contributions of Irish mathematicians and also the works of iconic mathematics writer [[Martin Gardner]]. 

In 2024 he received the [[Maths Week Ireland]] Award.<ref name=award>[https://www.irishtimes.com/science/2024/10/21/prof-colm-mulcahy-wins-2024-maths-week-ireland-award-for-exceptional-contribution-while-bringing-fun-to-maths/ Prof Colm Mulcahy wins 2024 Maths Week Ireland Award for exceptional contribution while bringing fun to maths] The Irish Times, Oct 21 2024</ref>

==Education and career==
Mulcahy got his BSc and MSc in mathematical science at [[University College Dublin]] in 1978 and 1979, and a PhD from [[Cornell University]] in 1985 where his advisor was [[Alex F. T. W. Rosenberg]].<ref name=allendoerfer/> From 1988 to 2020, he taught mathematics at [[Spelman College]], in [[Atlanta]], Georgia, and is now Professor Emeritus.<ref name=mathware/>  He served as chair of the department there from 2003 to 2006 and recently created the Archive of Spelman Mathematicians.<ref name=spellman>[http://www.spelman.edu/about-us/news-and-events/our-stories/stories/2016/01/29/professor-colm-mulcahy Spelman College] January 2016</ref> In 2014 he was one of the organizers of [[Mathematics Awareness Month]].<ref name=mathware>[http://www.mathaware.org/mam/2014/committee/ Mathematics Awareness Month 2014: Mathematics, Magic, and Mystery] Committee Members</ref> 

He has blogged for the [[Mathematical Association of America]], [[The Huffington Post]], [[Scientific American]], and (aperiodically) for The Aperiodical.<ref name=aperiodical>[http://aperiodical.com/ The Aperiodical]</ref> His puzzles have been featured in ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[The Guardian]]''.<ref=numberland>[https://www.theguardian.com/science/alexs-adventures-in-numberland/2014/feb/04/mathematics Algebra-cadabra! Here's a classic magic trick, and the mathematical secret behind it] by Alex Bellos, The Guardian, Tue 4 Feb 2014 </ref><ref name=celebrations1>''[http://blogs.scientificamerican.com/guest-blog/celebrations-of-mind-honor-mathe28099s-best-friend-martin-gardner/ Celebrations of Mind Honor Math’s Best Friend, Martin Gardner]'' by Colm Mulcahy, Scientific American, 29 October 2013</ref><ref name=stories>{{cite web |title=Stories by Colm Mulcahy |website=[[Scientific American]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230625050733/https://www.scientificamerican.com/author/colm-mulcahy/ |archive-date=25 June 2023 |url-status=live |url=http://www.scientificamerican.com/author/colm-mulcahy/}}</ref> Mulcahy serves on the Advisory Council of the [[Museum of Mathematics]] in New York City.<ref name= muma>[http://momath.org/about/advisory-council/ Museum of Mathematics: Advisory Council]</ref>  From January 2021 to December 2024, he was the Chair of [[Gathering 4 Gardner, Inc]].<ref name=g4gboard>[http://www.gathering4gardner.org/board-of-directors/ Gathering 4 Gardner: Board of Directors]</ref> He is the creator and curator of the ''Annals of Irish Mathematics and Mathematicians''.<ref name=annals>[http://www.mathsireland.ie/annals-of-irish-mathematics-mathematicians/maths-ireland Annals of Irish Mathematics & Mathematicians: Origin]</ref>

Mulcahy has an [[Erdős number|Erdös number]] of 2, as a result of a collaboration with [[Neil Calkin]].<ref name=erdos>[https://files.oakland.edu/users/grossman/enp/Erdos0.html Coauthors of Paul Erdos, see Neil Calkin] ''Gallia Est Omnis Divisa in Partes Quattuor'' by Neil Calkin and Colm Mulcahy, in ''The mathematics of various entertaining subjects: research in recreational math'', edited by Jennifer Elaine Beineke and Jason Rosenhouse, Princeton University Press, [2016] {{ISBN|0691164037}}</ref>

==Legacy of Martin Gardner==
Mulcahy was a friend of longtime Scientific American columnist [[Martin Gardner]] during the last decade of Gardner's life. Mulcahy is a mainstay of [[Gathering 4 Gardner]] (Vice-President 2016-2020, Chair 2021–2024), an organisation formed to honour the wide-ranging contributions made by the celebrated mathematician, skeptic, magician, philosopher, and writer. Usually shortened to G4G, it first met in 1993 and since 1996 meets every two years.<ref name=rodgers>[http://www.maa.org/news/math-news/tom-rodgers-organizer-of-gathering-for-gardner-and-celebration-of-mind-dies-at-67 Tom Rodgers, Organizer of Gathering for Gardner and Celebration of Mind, Dies at 67]</ref> In 2013 he created the official Martin Gardner site, and in 2013–2014 he chaired the Martin Gardner Centennial Committee.<ref name=MG_site>[http://martin-gardner.org/ official Martin Gardner site]</ref> Mulcahy has been particularly active in promoting an associated series of meetings known as [[Gathering_4_Gardner#Celebration_of_Mind_events|Celebration of Mind]], also inspired by the works of Gardner.<ref name=of_mind>[http://www.celebrationofmind.org/wordpress_site/?events=celebration-of-mind-with-colm-mulcahy Celebration of Mind with Colm Mulcahy]</ref> These days there are over 100 of these latter events every year, all around the world.<ref name=whowants>[http://aperiodical.com/2012/10/who-wants-to-host-a-celebration-of-mind-theres-still-time/#more-5802 Who wants to host a Celebration of Mind? There’s still time] by Colm Mulcahy, 19 October 2012</ref><ref name=celebrations>''[http://www.huffingtonpost.com/colm-mulcahy/martin-gardner-birthday_b_1956287.html Food for Thought: Savory Treats for the Mind From the Julia Child of Mathematics and Rationality]'' by Colm Mulcahy, ''HuffPost'', 10 December 2012</ref>

==Irish mathematicians and mathematics==
Mulcahy frequently writes about the culture and history of mathematics in Ireland.<ref name=huffy>''[http://www.huffingtonpost.com/colm-mulcahy/mathematical-and-poetic-offerings-from-the-land-of-saints-and-scholars_b_6888380.html%20Mathematical%20(and%20Poetic)%20Offerings%20From%20the%20Land%20of%20Saints%20and%20Scholars Mathematical (and Poetic) Offerings From the Land of Saints and Scholars]'' by Colm Mulcahy, ''HuffPost'', 23 May 2015</ref> He is active in both [[Maths Week Ireland]], the world's largest mathematics outreach program, and the [[Irish Mathematical Society]].<ref name=maths-week>{{cite news | url=http://www.irishtimes.com/news/science/more-than-250-000-people-to-take-part-in-maths-week-1.2387766 | first=Dick | last=Ahlstrom | title=More than 250,000 people to take part in Maths Week | newspaper=[[The Irish Times]] | date=11 October 2015 | accessdate=25 January 2018}}</ref> He is the creator and curator of the ''Annals of Irish Mathematics and Mathematicians'',<ref name=lynch>[https://www.irishtimes.com/science/2026/09/17/what-have-the-irish-ever-done-for-maths-on-counting-it-all-up-quite-a-lot-actually/ What have the Irish ever done for maths? On counting it all up - quite a lot, actually] by Peter Lynch,  17 sep 2026, Irish Times</ref> which chronicles four centuries of mathematical activity in Ireland, and has hosted monthly blogs since September 2016.<ref name=calendar>[http://www.mathsireland.ie/blog Blog Contents] Mathematics Ireland</ref> This is now sponsored by Maths Week Ireland, which has produced annual Irish Mathematics Calendars since 2016.<ref name=mathsire>[http://www.mathsireland.ie/annals-of-irish-mathematics-mathematicians/irish-maths-calendar Irish Maths Calendar] Mathematics Ireland</ref>

==Card magic==
Mulcahy is recognised as an authority on the mathematical principles and effects underlying cards tricks.<ref name=of_mind/> From 2004 to 2014 he authored ''Card Colm'', a column about mathematics and magic–especially card magic–for the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name=column>[http://www.maa.org/community/maa-columns MAA Columns: Card Colm by Colm Mulcahy] Mathematical Association of America</ref> Much of this work is collected in his book ''Mathematical Card Magic: Fifty-Two New Effects'' <ref name=tricks>''Mathematical Card Magic: Fifty-Two New Effects''  A K Peters/CRC Press (2013)  {{ISBN|1466509767}}</ref> He has appeared in Brady Haran's [[Numberphile]] web series.<ref name=numberphile>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4izjrtR8Ozg Little Fibs – Numberphile] 'Mathemagician' Colm Mulcahy, 2 June 2016</ref>

==Awards==
In 1997 Mulcahy received the MAA's [[Allendoerfer Award]] for excellence in expository writing for a paper on the basics of [[Wavelet transform#Wavelet compression|wavelet image compression]].<ref name=allendoerfer>[http://sections.maa.org/mddcva/Fall2013Meeting.php Carl B. Allendoerfer award: ''Plotting and Scheming with Wavelets'' by Colm Mulcahy]</ref>  An article he co-authored, on the centennial of Martin Gardner, was featured in the book, ''The Best Writing on Mathematics 2015''.<ref name=princeton>''[http://press.princeton.edu/TOCs/c10558.html The Best Writing on Mathematics 2015]'' Edited by Mircea Pitici, Princeton University Press, 2015, {{ISBN|0691169659}}</ref> 

In 2024 he received the [[Maths Week Ireland#Maths_Week_Ireland_Award|Maths Week Ireland Award]] for outstanding work in raising public awareness of mathematics. In his acceptance remarks, Mulcahy said,<ref name=darmody>[https://www.siliconrepublic.com/innovation/colm-mulcahy-maths-award-science-communication Prof Colm Mulcahy honoured for contributions to maths] by Jenny Darmody, [[Silicon Republic]], 18 Oct 2024</ref>

:Maths is a language that explains so much of the world around us: the sun, moon, planets and stars, hence the calendar and tides here on earth. That’s how it started for us humans; that and commerce. It’s about observation, curiosity and patterns, explaining symmetries and coincidences, navigating on earth and in space, and making reliable predictions.

==Personal==
Mulcahy was married to [[Victoria Powers|Vicki Powers]],<ref name=same_advisor>See the dedication to {{citation|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/my-heart-of-hearts_b_2641875|newspaper=Huffington Post|first=Colm|last=Mulcahy|title=In My Heart of Hearts: Valentine's Day Special|date=February 14, 2013}}</ref> an algebraic geometer and election theorist. They had the same doctoral advisor at Cornell, Alex F. T. W. Rosenberg.<ref name=geneal>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=30562 Victoria Ann Powers] at the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]</ref>
